exposure: Post-dated pregnancy (pregnancy lasting beyond 40 completed weeks of gestation)
cohort: The study included 146 pregnant individuals with pregnancies lasting beyond 40 completed weeks of gestation in a tertiary care centre.
finding: The study found a high rate of cesarean delivery (60%) in post-dated pregnancies, with fetal distress being the most common indication, and a significant proportion of both maternal (25%) and neonatal (45% admitted to NICU) complications.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was the mode of delivery in 60% of the patients.
